business.whatItDoes: Asian Paints Limited manufactures, distributes, and sells paints, coatings, home decor products, and bath and kitchen fittings. It also operates in industrial coatings through joint ventures and provides end-to-end home painting and décor services.

segments.name: Sleek - Kitchens and Wardrobes
segments.comment: Modular kitchen solutions, wardrobes, fitted furniture, and kitchen components.

segments.name: Bath Fittings and Sanitaryware
segments.comment: Premium and value bath fittings and sanitaryware through Bathsense and ESSESS.

scale: 3,264 business partners acknowledged Code of Conduct

guidance.statement: We should stay in the volume region of about 8-10% for the full FY27.
guidance.quote: At the current stage, we are looking at the band of 8-10% for the full FY27.
guidance.speaker: Amit Syngle

guidance.statement: We are still garnering around the guidance of 18-20% of our PBDIT margins holds.
guidance.quote: We are still garnering around the guidance of 18-20% of our PBDIT margins holds.
guidance.speaker: Amit Syngle

growthCommentary: Overall decorative volume growth was strong at about 9% for the quarter.
Decorative value grew at 16.6%, aided by a weighted price increase of about 6.8% and improved product mix.
Rural markets exhibited much better growth compared to urban markets.
B2B and industrial segments delivered robust performances, led by auto, marine, and general industrial growth.

pushback.question: Will you be happy with the 9% volume growth on a soft base of last year, and was there any negative impact of price hikes or regional factors?
pushback.answer: Demand conditions have been decent across all three months, though T1 and T2 cities saw lower growth compared to rural areas, and we landed within our predicted 8-10% band.

pushback.question: Given that costs went up by almost 25% against a 9-11% price increase, are we bracing for gross margin compression in Q2?
pushback.answer: While a large part of inflation will impact Q2, volatility also brings deflation in certain input categories, and our overall mix and sourcing efficiencies will govern margins.

pushback.question: How should one think about the product mix and the 7% pricing/value-volume gap this quarter given prior negative mix trends?
pushback.answer: The positive mix is driven by a strong focus on premiumization and newer innovations, and value will likely remain higher than volume until future pricing corrections.

guidance.statement: We are gunning for training almost 10 lakh people this year.
guidance.quote: and this year, as we kind of go ahead, we are gunning for training almost 10 lakh people.
guidance.speaker: Amit Syngle

growthCommentary: Decorative business achieved a high single-digit volume growth of 7.9% despite a compressed festive season and a prolonged monsoon.
Value growth for decorative was 2.8%, indicating a strong product mix.
Industrial and B2B segments performed exceptionally well, with PPGAP growing 17% and APPPG growing 16% in value terms.
Rural markets batted better than urban centers, aided by good rainfall and positive sentiment in November and December.

pushback.question: What are the reasons for the industry growth being so muted despite market leader activities and new player media spends?
pushback.answer: Management noted changing consumption patterns, a slight decline in painting frequency, fewer occasion-led paintings, and discretionary spending shifts toward travel, hospitality, and destination weddings.

pushback.question: Will the 4-5% volume-value gap persist, or is there a chance it will become zero without price changes?
pushback.answer: The gap is expected to remain around 4-5% due to the large underlying upgradation and economy segment mix, along with attendant products like undercoats.

pushback.question: Why are margins at the higher end of the guidance band despite muted growth and elevated competition, and is a price cut warranted?
pushback.answer: Margins are supported by internal structural cost efficiencies and raw material deflation rather than just pricing, and funds are used for brand building, services, and tech investments.

guidance.statement: Aiming for mid-single-digit value growth for the full year.
guidance.quote: We are looking at mid-single-digit value growth for the full year.
guidance.speaker: Amit Syngle

guidance.statement: Anticipate that the gap between volume and value will remain in the 4-5% zone.
guidance.quote: we would anticipate that the gap between the volume and the value would remain in that zone of about 4-5%.
guidance.speaker: Amit Syngle

guidance.statement: Maintain the PBDIT margin band of 18 to 20%.
guidance.quote: it is okay to maintain the whole guidance of 18 to 20% PBDIT margin band.
guidance.speaker: Amit Syngle

growthCommentary: Delivered a volume growth of 10.9% and value growth of 6% in Q2 FY26.
Driven by heavy brand spending, new product innovation, and regionalization initiatives.
Supported by good performance in the Prelux category in emulsions and strong international and industrial businesses.
Raw material prices remained benign with deflation of 1.6% in Q2.

pushback.question: What has been your reaction to the 10% free grammage in different SKUs by a competitor, and is intensity waning?
pushback.answer: Asian Paints focuses on fundamentals, brand building, and premium/luxury finishes rather than just discounting, which reduces retailer turnover.

pushback.question: Why is the volume-value gap lower than historical trends, and will it reduce?
pushback.answer: A balanced approach across economy, mid-level, and luxury segments is maintained to avoid losing out in large volume categories like economy.

pushback.question: Given benign raw material costs, are you comfortable landing at the higher end of the 18-20% margin band?
pushback.answer: Management is comfortable maintaining the 18-20% band given meaningful investments in marketing, technology, and higher competitive intensity.

synthesis.take: Asian Paints experienced a margin compression down to 16% OPM in Sep 2026 despite strong 16.9% revenue growth, reflecting rising input cost inflation. Management maintains volume growth targets while navigating shifts toward rural demand and increasing competitive intensity.

promises.delivered: FY26 operating profit margin reported at 19%.

narrative.claim: Management stated that rural markets exhibited much better growth compared to urban markets.
narrative.numbers: Reported strong performance in rural areas helping offset slower urban T1 and T2 city growth.

narrative.claim: Management maintained the PBDIT margin band of 18% to 20% throughout multiple quarters.
narrative.numbers: Operating margins dropped to 16% in Sep 2026, falling below the guided band.

narrative.claim: Management highlighted strong volume growth of 10.9% and value growth of 6% in Q2 FY26.
narrative.numbers: Consolidated revenue for Sep 2025 was ₹8,531 crore, showing a 6.3% YoY increase.

bull.point: Industrial and B2B segments delivered robust performances with PPGAP growing 17% and APPPG growing 16% in value.
Strong cash conversion capacity with 109% of 5-year profit turned into operating cash.
Consistent decorative volume growth, achieving 9% in Q1 FY27 and landing within the guided 8-10% band.

bear.point: Operating margins compressed to 16% in Sep 2026 due to raw material cost inflation.
Discretionary spending shifts and changing consumption patterns have created a persistent volume-value gap.
Debt-to-equity ratio increased from 0.12 in Mar 2025 to 0.21 by Sep 2026.

watch: Monitor whether operating margins recover back to the 18-20% guided band.
Track the persistence of the volume-value gap in subsequent quarters.
Observe urban versus rural market demand divergences.
